newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-IRABU PROMOTED TO AA, SET TO START FRIDAY.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-IRABU PROMOTED TO AA, SET TO START FRIDAY.

text.p: Japanese pitcher Hideki Irabu, who did not allow a run in two starts for the New York Yankees' Class-A Tampa farm team, Monday was promoted to Norwich of the AA Eastern League and was expected to start Friday, the Yankees announced.
Irabu, who signed a four-year, $12.8 million contract with the Yankees in late May, allowed just four hits and struck out 12 in his first two starts in the United States.
In his second minor league start, the Japanese star threw five scoreless innings against St. Petersburg, scattering three hits. Irabu threw 40 of his 60 pitches for strikes.

Touted as the Japanese Nolan Ryan, the hard-throwing Irabu pitched four scoreless innings, allowing one hit with no walks and six strikeouts in his Tampa debut. He threw 42 pitches, all clocked consistently near 100 miles per hour (161 kph).

The right-hander was also expected to pitch for Columbus, the Yankees' Triple-A farm team -- the highest level in minor league ball -- before joining the Yankees sometime around the July All-Star break, if all goes according to schedule.
The Yanks signed the 28-year-old Irabu after striking a deal with the San Diego Padres, who owned his rights through an agreement with his Japanese team, the Chiba Lotte Marines.
The Padres were forced to deal the potential star hurler after he insisted that he would not play for any U.S. major league team other than the Yankees.
Irabu, known for this strikeout prowess, led the Japanese Pacific League with a 2.40 ERA last season.

When he joins the Yankees, he will become the fourth Japanese player in the major leagues, joining pitchers Hideo Nomo of the Los Angeles Dodgers, Shigetoshi Hasegawa of the Anaheim Angels and Takashi Kashiwada of the New York Mets.
